The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) says it has received 78,112 newly produced Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) for distribution across the 17 Local Government Areas (LGAs) of Enugu State, ruling out collection by proxy. INEC Resident Electoral Commissioner in the state, Dr Chukwuemeka Chukwu, disclosed this while briefing journalists on Tuesday in Enugu. Chukwu said the PVCs would be made available to their rightful owners in line with the commission’s established procedures. He said the PVC remained an essential requirement for eligible registered voters to exercise their civic responsibility during elections. According to him, without the card, eligible voters cannot exercise their right to vote in any election organised by INEC. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources “The commission is therefore committed to ensuring that all PVCs received are properly accounted for and made available to their rightful owners in line with the commission’s established procedures. “I am pleased to announce that INEC Enugu State has so far received a total of 78,112 newly produced Permanent Voter Cards in three batches as follows: “First Batch: 17,220 PVCs. (transfers and replacement across all categories). Second Batch: 20,137 PVCs. (first phase registration), Third Batch: 40,755 PVCs. (second phase registration); total PVCs received: 78,112,” he said. The REC gave a breakdown of the PVCs allocated to each of the 17 LGAs and urged affected registrants to visit their respective INEC LGA offices to collect their cards promptly. Chukwu appealed to political parties, community leaders, traditional rulers, religious leaders, civil society organisations and the media to assist INEC in sensitising citizens on the importance of PVC collection and active participation in the electoral process. He also reiterated INEC’s commitment to conducting free, fair, credible, inclusive and transparent elections in the state and across the country. Chukwu said the commission would continue to work closely with relevant stakeholders to ensure that all electoral activities were conducted in accordance with the law and established guidelines. He assured residents that the commission would continue to discharge its responsibilities with diligence, transparency and professionalism. (NAN) Kindly share this story:
